title: acquire-v4 promotion prerequisites: live tap-distance instrumentation

what_was_built.summary: Always-on target-lock telemetry (schema v1, D-043 conventions) in the apps/mobile guided-capture target-lock flow. Whenever the user taps a start region, the capture persists a `targetLock` record alongside the clip payload (same path as `targetSeed`): tap point, acquired track's torso center at the lock frame, tap-to-track distance, time-to-lock, ambiguity flags/duration, lock source, and lock outcome ('locked' | 'no_lock'). Acquisition behavior is UNCHANGED: the instrument only observes the shipped D-027 state machine; no thresholds, states, or lock decisions were touched.

files.apps/mobile/ios/LocalPods/PickleNative/S: Instrument state (first/last acquisition frame ms, ambiguity-entered ms, lock record), lockTarget now receives the frame timestamp for the record, targetLockTelemetryPayload() builds the schema-v1 payload attached in finishSuccess next to targetSeed.
files.apps/mobile/src/camera/capture.ts: TargetLockTelemetryV1 type, TARGET_LOCK_PARAMS_V1 (frozen shipped D-027 constants: startRegionRadius .17, occupancyFramesToLock 9, sustainedGestureFrames 5, ambiguityTimeoutMs 3000, gestureElevationThreshold .03), and boundary validation: distance must recompute from the recorded points (tolerance 1e-6), locked records must match the clip targetSeed exactly (torso + source), gesture/timeout locks require the ambiguity flag, timeout locks require ambiguityDurationMs >= 3000, no_lock records may carry no lock evidence or seed, params must equal the frozen v1 constants, imported video rejects the field.
files.apps/mobile/__tests__/cameraCapture.test: 11 new boundary tests (accept locked / no-lock / pre-instrument captures; reject fabricated distance, seed disagreement, missing ambiguity flags, sub-timeout timeout locks, drifted params, malformed points/sources/outcomes, no-lock with lock evidence, imported video with targetLock).

what_was_built.replay_readiness: A future replay can run the D-027 gate pattern for acquire-v4's tap-centered lock gate directly from persisted captures: tapToLockDistance is the acquire-v4 gate signal (bench separation at .05: correct instant locks <= .04 in 23/25, wrong grabs >= .056 in 8/9, per packages/swing-lab taReplay comments), and lockSource/ambiguity flags map onto taReplay's event model.

exact_numbers.mobile_jest: 225/225 tests green, 30 suites (was 214 canonical; +11 new targetLock boundary tests)
exact_numbers.pnpm_r_typecheck: all packages pass (analysis-pipeline, vision-geometry, swing-lab rebuilt; exit 0)
exact_numbers.acquire_v4_bench_context: correct .863 / contested wrong .167 at n=54 (HANDOFF_V3, unchanged; not re-measured here)

honest_negatives: No live measurement exists yet: this session ran on Linux with no iPhone; the Swift instrumentation compiles only in an iOS build (not verifiable here) and has produced zero real telemetry records. The n=54 bench numbers are the only acquire-v4 evidence; nothing new was measured.

The Swift side has no unit tests (repo has no XCTest harness for GuidedCaptureViewController); correctness of the native payload is enforced indirectly by the TS boundary validation, which will reject a malformed native record at capture time.

apps/mobile `npx eslint` crashes on ALL files (including untouched App.tsx) from a preexisting eslint 8/9 hoisting conflict with the root pnpm workspace; lint could not be run. tsc + jest were the mandated checks and are green.

Telemetry timestamps are camera-clock durations only (timeToLockMs, ambiguityDurationMs); absolute lock timestamps are not persisted because the lock precedes the exported clip window and rebasing would produce negative, misleading values.
remains_blocked: acquire-v4 promotion: still requires (1) real live captures carrying this telemetry from device use, and (2) the locked_test one-shot, which is Mac-gated (Apple Vision pose extraction is macOS-only). Neither is possible in this Linux environment.
The D-027-style gate replay over live tapToLockDistance values cannot run until live captures exist.
